results.body:
Found while verifying the source spelling for #406 — the raw TOGO capture is
tracked, so the import can be compared against it directly.

## The substitution

`data/raw/togo/togo_media.json` records each component's own unit. Comparing
2,900 matched TOGO media, component by component:

```
comparable rows                                32,841
source unit is a VOLUME (ml, ml/l, L, ul)       3,808
  -> recorded as G_PER_L                        3,803
  -> recorded as ML_PER_L or L                      2
```

The unit is not converted, it is **replaced**. `CultureMech:008849`
(`TOGO:M2262`, PCR-S11 medium) side by side with its source:

| ingredient | TOGO says | record says |
|---|---|---|
| Seawater (autoclaved) | 1000 **ml** | 1000 **G_PER_L** |
| Trace metals 'Gaffron+Se' | 0.5 **ml/l** | 0.5 **G_PER_L** |
| 50mM NaH2PO4 | 100 **ml** | 100 **G_PER_L** |
| 0.1N HCl | 40 **ml** | 40 **G_PER_L** |
| (NH4)2SO4 | 400 uM | 400 MICROMOLAR ✅ |
| Vitamin B12 | 10 ug/L | 10 MICROG_PER_L ✅ |
| Hepes | 119.15 g | 119.15 G_PER_L ✅ |

Molar and mass units convert correctly. Only volumes are mislabelled, and the
schema already has `ML_PER_L` and `L` for them.

## Where it is and is not defensible

**Water — 2,579 rows.** Water's density is 1, so `1000 ml -> 1000 g/L` is
numerically near-exact. Ugly, and it is what feeds `WATER_AS_VOLUME` in
`audit-concentration-plausibility`, but not a wrong quantity.

**Everything else — 1,224 rows across 751 records.** The density is not 1, so
the number itself is wrong:

| ingredient | rows | density | error |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| `HCl (25%; 7.7 M)` | 72 | ~1.12 | 12% low |
| `Methanol` | 26 | 0.792 | 26% high |
| `Glycerol` | 21 | 1.26 | 21% low |
| `Tween 80` | 20 | 1.06 | |
| `Ethanol` | 14 | 0.789 | 27% high |
| `Sol. 1`, `Artificial seawater`, `Seawater`, `NaOH 1 N`, ... | | | |

`0.5 ml/l` of a trace-metal stock recorded as `0.5 g/L` is not a rounding
difference — it is a different physical quantity, and nothing downstream can
tell.

## No gate sees the non-water half

`audit-concentration-plausibility` has `WATER_AS_VOLUME` (water >= 1000 G_PER_L),
which is why the water rows are already inside #150's backlog. Methanol at
`792 G_PER_L`, glycerol at `50 G_PER_L` and HCl at `40 G_PER_L` match no
detector — not a trace salt, not an indicator, not water.

## Suggested

1. Map source volume units onto `ML_PER_L` / `L` at import rather than
   defaulting to `G_PER_L`. The enum values exist.
2. Repair the 1,224 non-water rows from the tracked raw capture, which holds
   the original unit — so this is a relabelling, not a re-derivation, and needs
   no source lookup.
3. Decide the water case deliberately: `2,579` rows are numerically fine and
   semantically wrong, and they currently inflate `WATER_AS_VOLUME`.
4. Check whether the same substitution exists in the other volume-bearing
   importers (MediaDive, KOMODO, JCM) — this was found by comparing against a
   tracked raw capture, which not every source has.

Related: #150 (the plausibility backlog the water half sits in), #381 (absolute
amounts with no representable unit), #394 (a different import-time arithmetic
defect), #406 (the record this was found from).
results.title: TOGO import substitutes G_PER_L for volume units: 3,803 rows, of which 1,224 are non-water and numerically wrong

results.body:
Found while triaging the ingredient labels MIM cannot resolve
(MediaIngredientMech `scripts/triage_culturemech_residual.py`). 24 distinct
`preferred_term` values covering **618 recipe mentions** are not ingredient names at all.
The damage is in `data/normalized_yaml/` itself, not introduced by the occurrence
exporter, so it dates from recipe ingestion.

Two distinct defects.

## 1. Field swap: the quantity is in `preferred_term`, the name is in `notes` (497 mentions)

```
CultureMech:000001  preferred_term: "1"  notes: "Original amount: DYIII Medium"
CultureMech:000001  preferred_term: "2"  notes: "Original amount: Pea"
CultureMech:000002  preferred_term: "1"  notes: "Original amount: CR1 Soil"
CultureMech:000002  preferred_term: "2"  notes: "Original amount: MgCO3(MCIB CB486)"
```

`preferred_term` holds the ingredient's list index while the actual name sits in `notes`.
**All 497 of these carry an `Original amount:` note, so the name is recoverable for 100% of
them** -- this is a remapping, not a re-scrape. Affected values are the bare numbers 1-13.

## 2. A Python list repr split on commas (121 mentions)

| mentions | preferred_term |
|---:|---|
| 75 | `'Iron(III` |
| 13 | `'Fe(III` |
| 8 | `'Chromium(III` |
| 6 | `'(S` |
| 2 | `'Manganese(IV` |
| 2 | `'(9Z` |
| 1 | `'Nickel(II` |
| 1 | `'Cyanocob(III` |

Note the leading apostrophe on each. From `data/normalized_yaml/`, verbatim:

    - preferred_term: '''Iron(III'
      concentration:
        value: '0.04994'

That apostrophe is a Python string quote, and every value truncates at the first comma
inside a chemical name -- `Iron(III), citrate` and `(9Z,12Z)-octadecadienoate` split at
their internal comma. A `str()` of a list was written where the list elements were meant,
then re-split on `", "`. The oxidation-state Roman numerals and stereodescriptors are
exactly the names that contain commas, which is why they are the ones that broke.

Unlike defect 1 these are lossy -- the tail of each name became a separate fragment or was
dropped -- so they need re-derivation from the source recipe rather than a field move.

## Why it matters

These 618 mentions are permanently unresolvable against MIM: no ontology will ever contain
a term called `1` or `'Iron(III`, so they sit in MIM's residual forever and inflate the
apparent size of the ingredient-grounding backlog. MIM's triage now classifies them as
`NOISE` and routes them out of the grounding work, but the fix belongs here.

Evidence table: MIM `reports/culturemech_residual_triage.tsv`, rows whose `bucket` starts
with `NOISE`.
results.title: 618 ingredient mentions carry parse damage as their preferred_term; all 497 numeric ones are recoverable

results.body:
The residual of #387, now that both of its populations are repaired. **One row,
corpus-wide.**

```
CultureMech:008849   data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/pcr_s11_medium.yaml
  ingredients[4].preferred_term = "Trace metals 'Gaffron\xad+Se'"
                                                        ^^^^^^ U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN
  concentration: 0.5 G_PER_L
  media_term: TOGO:M2262 — "PCR-S11 medium"
```

## Why it is not the same defect as the rest of #387

#387's two populations were parser damage — a field swap (497 numeric
`preferred_term`s, fixed in #378) and truncation at a parenthesis (111 names,
fixed in #391). Both destroyed information.

This one loses nothing. `Trace metals 'Gaffron+Se'` is a real name with a
**discretionary hyphen** inside it: U+00AD renders as nothing unless a line
breaks there, so the string looks correct in every editor and report while
being a different string to every matcher. It is almost certainly a
soft-wrap artifact from the source page carried through the import verbatim.

Measured across the whole corpus, this is the only ingredient name containing
any invisible character — soft hyphen, ZWSP, ZWNJ, ZWJ, NBSP, BOM, word joiner
or line/paragraph separator. So it is a single record, not a class.

## Consequence

The name cannot ground: no matcher normalises U+00AD, so it fails MIM's label
index and every exact-match path. It is one of the 3,217 unresolvable names that
`just audit-ungrounded-ingredients` reports.

## Suggested

Delete the soft hyphen. That is not a curation decision — U+00AD carries no
semantic content in a chemical name and its removal cannot change what the name
denotes.

Worth checking the source (`TOGO:M2262`) first to confirm the intended spelling,
and worth deciding whether a normalisation step should strip zero-width and
discretionary characters at import so the next one does not need an issue.

"Gaffron" here is the trace-element solution of Gaffron; `+Se` marks the
selenium-supplemented variant.
results.title: The last #387 parse-damaged ingredient name: a soft hyphen inside Trace metals 'Gaffron+Se'
